title: Why the Moon Is Inside Earth's Atmosphere
topic: Earth's geocorona, a thin hydrogen cloud, reaches about 630,000 km (ESA/NASA SOHO, 2019), almost twice the Moon's distance, so the Moon moves inside it; Apollo 16 photographed it from the Moon in 1972; Artemis II (April 2026, 406,771 km) stayed inside it

beats.narration: No human has ever left Earth's atmosphere. Not even the astronauts who flew around the Moon this year.
Wait. The Moon is in space!
We say space starts a hundred kilometers up. But Earth's air doesn't just stop. It fades into a thin cloud of hydrogen.
phrases: It fades into a thin cloud

beats.narration: Old data from the SOHO spacecraft showed that cloud reaches six hundred and thirty thousand kilometers. Almost twice as far as the Moon.

beats.narration: So the Moon flies through Earth's atmosphere. Apollo 16 astronauts photographed its glow from the Moon, never knowing they were inside it.
In April, Artemis 2 flew humans farther than ever. Over four hundred thousand kilometers. Still inside.
Out there it's so thin, we'd call it a vacuum. But where it touches the Moon, it's leaving a mark.
